'''Natalia G. Berloff''' is a Russian professor of [[applied mathematics]] at the [[University of Cambridge]]. She is interested in fluid dynamics, particularly [[superfluidity]] and the dynamics of quantum fluids. Her research includes the use of [[polariton]]s to simulate structures such as the [[classical XY model]].

==Early life and education==
Berloff grew up in Russia.<ref name=plus/> She earned her undergraduate degrees of BS (1991) and MS (1992) from [[Moscow State University|Lomonosov Moscow State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Natalia Berloff – russaccom.org |url=https://russaccom.org/dr-natalia-berloff-2/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=russaccom.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=π-Computing - Team |url=https://www.pi-computing.org/team |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=www.pi-computing.org |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2014-04-02 |title=Skoltech {{!}} Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology |url=https://www.skoltech.ru/en/2014/04/prof-natalia-berloff-to-serve-as-the-dean-of-faculty/ |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=Skoltech {{!}} Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology |language=en-US}}</ref> She earned her Ph.D. from [[Florida State University]] in 1996, under the supervision of [[Louis Norberg Howard]].<ref name=mgp>{{mathgenealogy|id=87086}}</ref>

==Career==
Berloff was a UC President's Research Fellow in the Department of Mathematics of the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] from 1997 to 1999, and continued there as PIC Assistant Professor from 1999 to 2002, when she became a Fellow of [[Jesus College, Cambridge]], and a faculty member in the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics at Cambridge, where she is now Professor in Applied Mathematics.<ref name="plus">{{citation|url=https://plus.maths.org/content/women-mathematics-natalia-berloff|title=Natalia Berloff|journal=Plus Magazine|date=12 April 2017}}</ref> Berloff  is the principal investigator of the Pi-computing team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=π-Computing - Team |url=https://www.pi-computing.org/team |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=www.pi-computing.org |language=en-US}}</ref> Berloff describes herself as a fluid dynamicist, and she is interested in describing the dynamics of physical systems, such as quantum fluids, [[superfluidity]], and [[Bose–Einstein condensate|Bose-Einstein condensate]].<ref name="plus" /> Her research includes the use of [[polariton]]s to simulate structures such as the [[classical XY model]].<ref name="UoC">{{citation |title=Natalia G Berloff |year=2012 |url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/ngb23/ |publisher=University of Cambridge}}</ref> 

From 2013 to 2016 Berloff  took a leave of absence from Cambridge to serve as a Professor and Director of Photonics and Quantum Materials Program at the [[Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology]] in Russia.<ref name="UoC" />

In 2005 Berloff was awarded the Pilkington Prize by the Cambridge Centre of Teaching and Learning.<ref name=":0" />
